hypotheses.statement: If one case RNA species acts as a scaffold and another as a weaker-binding adsorbent, composition-dependent adsorption/wetting at interfaces inside a scaffold-rich network could stabilize RNA-poor internal domains that appear as cavities. This extends the external/coexisting-interface relation reported for a different two-RNA/PEG system to internal domains in this transcribing condensate. Neither the case species roles nor internal cavity formation is established. At fixed reaction chemistry, directly measured RNA loading should change species-resolved interface enrichment; cavity incidence/area should covary only if the proposed internal-domain bridge is correct.

The phase endpoints are not comparable to the imaging reaction or its mixture range, or relative selectivity is constant under matched conditions; cavities instead arise from amplification carryover or another reaction-state change independently of composition-driven wetting. Population changes and image segmentation may also alter summary f without within-droplet cavity formation.

gaps.description: Determine whether measured RNA composition changes partitioning or interface wetting under matched conditions and whether that predicts internal cavities. Neither the composition response nor the internal-domain bridge is identified by current evidence.
No mapping from bulk phase concentrations/volumes or interfacial enrichment to image f, and no causal separation from carryover or population/measurement alternatives.
